title: Cartilage-protective effects of lopinavir/ritonavir: in vitro and in silico exploration of the HIF-1alpha/SOX9/IL-1beta pathway.
authors: Ozbek, Hanefi; Yilmaz, Ibrahim; Akyuz, Asli; Pehlivanoglu, Suray; Sirin, Duygu Yasar; Albayrak, Mehmet; Yilmaz, Omer Faruk
journal: Journal of orthopaedic surgery and research
one_liner_zh: 该文研究洛匹那韦/利托那韦对软骨细胞的保护作用，涉及HIF-1alpha/SOX9/IL-1beta通路，虽含分子对接但对象为药物-蛋白，非蛋白质-DNA互作，且无AI或MD方法，与本课题关联微弱。
abstract: BACKGROUND: This study aimed to investigate the effects of Lopinavir/Ritonavir (Lop/r) on chondrocyte structure and extracellular matrix (ECM) integrity, as well as its impact on key proteins involved in anabolic and catabolic pathways, using both in vitro and in silico approaches. METHODS: Drug-target interaction networks were constructed through bioinformatics analyses, and molecular docking was performed. Human primary chondrocytes were treated with Lop/r, and untreated cells served as controls. Cell viability, proliferation, and protein expression levels were assessed using standard in vitro techniques, including spectrophotometric assays and Western blotting. RESULTS: Molecular docking analyses revealed strong binding affinities between Lop/r and osteoarthritis-related targets such as HIF-1alpha, EP300, TNF, IL-6, KCNA5, and IL-1beta, suggesting modulation of hypoxia, inflammatory, and epigenetic pathways. In vitro, Lop/r did not alter chondrocyte morphology or ECM structure and was not cytotoxic (p < 0.05). However, it significantly reduced the expression of critical proteins including HIF-1alpha, SOX9, and IL-1beta (p < 0.05). CONCLUSION: These findings suggest that Lop/r may exert regulatory effects on cartilage-related molecular pathways and holds promise as a repurposed therapeutic agent for osteoarthritis. Further studies are warranted to confirm its potential in clinical applications.
abstract_zh: 背景：本研究旨在通过体外（in vitro）和计算机模拟（in silico）方法，探讨洛匹那韦/利托那韦（Lopinavir/Ritonavir, Lop/r）对软骨细胞结构和细胞外基质（extracellular matrix, ECM）完整性的影响，及其对合成代谢和分解代谢通路中关键蛋白的作用。方法：通过生物信息学分析构建药物-靶点相互作用网络，并进行分子对接（molecular docking）。人原代软骨细胞经Lop/r处理，未处理细胞作为对照。采用标准体外技术，包括分光光度法测定和Western blotting，评估细胞活力、增殖及蛋白表达水平。结果：分子对接分析显示，Lop/r与骨关节炎相关靶点如HIF-1alpha、EP300、TNF、IL-6、KCNA5和IL-1beta之间具有强结合亲和力，提示其对缺氧、炎症和表观遗传通路的调节作用。体外实验中，Lop/r未改变软骨细胞形态或ECM结构，且无细胞毒性（p < 0.05）。然而，它显著降低了关键蛋白的表达，包括HIF-1alpha、SOX9和IL-1beta（p < 0.05）。结论：这些发现表明，Lop/r可能对软骨相关分子通路发挥调节作用，并有望作为骨关节炎的再利用治疗药物。需进一步研究以确认其在临床应用中的潜力。
